newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds stay hostage to U.S. developments.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds stay hostage to U.S. developments.

text.p: *Australian bonds remain hostage to developments in the United States in the absence of local incentives, finishing Wednesday's session with only modest yield falls.
*Local Feb retail trade, building approvals due Friday.
Australian bonds remain hostage to developments in the U.S. in the absence of local incentives, finishing Wednesday's session with only modest yield falls.
However, U.S. Treasuries could face a quiet session later today as the market prepares for Friday's key non-farm payrolls report for March and with no major data due later today.

Local bonds took their slightly firmer tone from minor price gains in the U.S. on Tuesday following the National Association of Purchasing Management index for March, which extended into Tokyo trading, but the market failed to get too carried away by the move, traders said.
"Local interest remains fairly dire. You still have people away for Easter, and nothing really to look forward to until Friday's retail data," one trader said.

February retail trade and building approvals are due at the end of the week, but even then the reaction to these partial indicators could be limited with the major U.S. jobs data to be released later that day, traders said.

The balance of goods and services for February are due Thursday, but the data is unlikely to stir the market from its U.S. watch. Economists' expectations are fairly wide-ranging, from down A$200 million to up A$250 million.

Meanwhile, sources close to the Industrial Relations Commission said a verdict on the "living wage" claim would not be made this week. The market has been waiting for a decision for some weeks as it will give a guide to future wage inflation.
Overseas, the U.S. March NAPM index showed a fall in the prices component, helping to soothe the shock of a rise to 55.0 in the overall index, its highest level since February 1995.

The BOJ's quarterly Tankan survey showed that manufacturers' business sentiment and the June diffussion index remained weak, sparking a steep rally in JGBS and kept Australia's yield differential to Japan attractive for Japanese investors.

Local yield differentials were little changed to the U.S., but narrowed again against Canadian debt which remains weighed down by a weakening Canadian dollar. The Canadian currency neared a two-year low against the U.S. unit on Tuesday, undermined by the expectation that the Fed will tighten again.
The June 10-year bond contract failed to sustain a break above 91.800 resistance after rebounding from a SYCOM contract low of 91.700.
